visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Harbour's enterprise value is €1.5bn and its EBITDA €150m. The buyer expects €50m a year of savings. What multiple is it effectively paying?

options.text: 6x
8x

questions.explain: Add the savings to EBITDA: €1,500m ÷ €200m = 7.5x. Without them it's 10x, two turns above the peers' 8x.
questions.explain_at: Seven and a half times. Below the peers

questions.q: What should the first sentence of a deal pitch say?

options.text: Who bought what, for how much, when
The background, in the order it happened
Your view on whether it was a good deal
The trends in the buyer's industry

questions.explain: Lead with the headline. Chronology is how you remember a deal, not how you tell it; the view comes last.
questions.explain_at: Lead with the headline, one sentence

questions.q: An interviewer asks whether a deal was a good one. What does a strong view answer?

options.text: Yes, if the target is a good company
Whether the buyer's shares went up
Whether its industry is growing
Good for whom, at this price, why

questions.explain: A good company at too high a price is a bad deal. A view says who it's good for, at this price, and gives one reason.
questions.explain_at: A good company and a good deal aren't the same thing

questions.q: Guidewire may pay up to $2.1bn for hyperexponential. What is the $400m on top of the $1.7bn base price?

options.text: Part of the cash paid at closing
An earn-out tied to revenue targets
Debt that Guidewire takes on
Shares given to the founders

questions.explain: It's contingent consideration, paid only if hx reaches recurring revenue targets. So $2.1bn is the most the deal could cost, not the price.

questions.q: The interviewer asks for hx's revenue, which hasn't been disclosed. What do you do?

options.text: Give a round number that sounds right
Switch to talking about the price
Say so, then use what is disclosed
Say you don't know and stop there

questions.explain: An invented number won't survive the follow-up. Say it isn't disclosed, then use what is, such as Guidewire's 6.5 points of extra ARR growth.
questions.explain_at: Neither company has disclosed H-X's revenue
